title: The screens that were missing — sending, sent, failed, setting up

steps.headline: 24. Setting up says which step it is on.
steps.changed: The screen names the step running now — downloading the project, then its five parts, then installing what they need — instead of one unchanging line.
steps.notice: A setup that takes minutes looks like it is working rather than stuck.
steps.risk: The steps are the real ones, but nothing is downloaded yet.

steps.headline: 25. When it finishes, it says where your project is and offers to open it.
steps.changed: A finished setup names the folder it created and gives you one action to open it, with Not now beside it.
steps.notice: You are told where it went, and that nothing else on your computer changed.
steps.risk: The folder is an example; nothing is created yet.

steps.headline: 26. If setup fails, it says why and offers to carry on.
steps.changed: The reason comes from the step that failed. Retry resumes, Report bug files it. The old screen's only button here was Done.
steps.notice: You keep what already downloaded, and you are not sent back to the start.
steps.risk: The reason shown is an example failure.

steps.path: Settings → Development → Report a Bug or Request a Feature
steps.headline: 27. Sending a ticket says it is sending.
steps.changed: A short step between pressing Submit and being told the outcome. There was nothing here before — the button simply did nothing.
steps.notice: You can tell the press registered, so you do not press it twice.
steps.risk: Nothing is sent to GitHub yet.

steps.path: Settings → Development → Report a Bug or Request a Feature
steps.headline: 28. A submitted ticket gives you its link.
steps.changed: The screen confirms it is submitted, repeats that anyone can read it, and shows the address so you can follow it.
steps.notice: You leave with a link rather than wondering whether it worked.

steps.path: Settings → Development → Report a Bug or Request a Feature
steps.headline: 29. A ticket that could not be sent keeps every word you typed.
steps.changed: The failure sits above your draft, which is untouched, with one Retry. The Submit button is hidden while it shows, so there is one way to try again, not two.
steps.notice: Nothing you wrote is lost, and you can edit before trying again.
steps.risk: The reason shown is an example failure.

steps.path: Settings → Development → Report a Bug or Request a Feature
steps.headline: 30. Attaching files hands you over to GitHub, and says so.
steps.changed: When you choose to attach screenshots or files, the ticket is not submitted here — it opens in your browser with everything you wrote, for you to attach and submit there.
steps.notice: You know the ticket is not filed yet and that finishing it is your next step.
